summary: Verified the /auth/callback consolidation + stale-origin hardening for Supabase auth redirects. Repo-wide grep confirms ZERO 'lovable'/'lovableproject' occurrences and no '.lovable.app', '.vercel.app', or '.emergentagent.com' used as auth redirects (the one '.vercel.app' hit is inside the stale-origin unit test, which is intentional; the .emergentagent.com hits are inside .emergent/cron webhook config, unrelated to auth). All 5 vitest tests pass across 3 files, including the new assertion that even when window.location.origin is stubbed to https://old-preview.vercel.app/ every auth redirect helper still resolves to https://asvior.app (with getPasswordResetRedirectUrl explicitly returning https://asvior.app/auth/callback?type=recovery). Web routes /, /auth, /reset-password, /visa-check, /countries, /budget-planner all 200. New /auth/callback route serves HTML 200 with title 'Signing you in — Asvior' for the no-param, ?error=..., and ?type=recovery variants, then client-side redirects to /auth (verified via Playwright — after visiting /auth/callback the browser lands on the Welcome-back sign-in card). /api/health returns 503 with the exact required JSON; POST /api/chat with a valid messages array returns 500 'Missing AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY' (designed). supabase/config.toml site_url=https://asvior.app and additional_redirect_urls contains both https://asvior.app/auth/callback and asvior://asvior.app/auth/callback and their ?type=recovery variants. AndroidManifest.xml still declares BOTH the asvior:// scheme intent-filter and the autoVerify https://asvior.app App-Link intent-filter. src/routes/auth.tsx still passes getEmailVerificationRedirectUrl()/getPasswordResetRedirectUrl() to Supabase; src/lib/native-init.ts no longer calls exchangeCodeForSession directly (only navigates the deep-link path — code-exchange is now solely handled by /auth/callback, so exchange happens exactly once on both web and native).

endpoint_verification.GET /auth: 200 (sign-in form visible, email input present, title 'Sign in — Asvior')
endpoint_verification.GET /auth/callback: 200, title 'Signing you in — Asvior', renders auth-callback-card, then client-redirects to /auth (verified in-browser)
endpoint_verification.GET /auth/callback?error=access_denied&e: 200, renders callback card, then redirects to /auth
endpoint_verification.GET /auth/callback?type=recovery: 200 (no code -> treated as invalid, redirects to /auth as designed)

vitest_results: 3 files, 5 tests, all passed (auth-redirects incl. stale-origin case, combobox-viewport, runtime-health)

grep_verification..vercel.app hostname: only inside src/lib/auth-redirects.test.ts (the STALE-ORIGIN stub) — intentional
grep_verification..emergentagent.com: only inside .emergent/cron/webhook-crons — unrelated to auth redirects

critical_code_review_comments: auth.callback.tsx uses a module-scoped Set<string> `processedCodes` to guard against double-exchange. This is correct within a single JS context (single tab / single native cold-start). If the user opens the confirmation link twice (e.g. deep-link cold start + browser tab), each context has its own Set — Supabase will return 'invalid grant' on the second exchange and the catch branch will toast and bounce to /auth, which is acceptable UX.

auth.callback.tsx: when search.type === 'recovery' and no session was established, code path currently allows the recovery branch even without a session (because of the `&& !search.type` guard on the 'invalid link' short-circuit). That means visiting /auth/callback?type=recovery with no code will still forward to /reset-password. Empirically verified — the URL still redirects (through the /reset-password screen which itself will bounce authless users). Consider tightening to also require a session for recovery. Not a blocker.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (web-layer regression scope only; Android runtime out-of-scope, no SDK/emulator)
